subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A key reason for performing a warm-up before exercise is to:
options: Increase muscle temperature and reduce injury risk
questions.explain: A warm-up raises muscle temperature and prepares the body, reducing the risk of injury.

questions.q: Specificity as a principle of training means:
options: Fitness is lost when you stop
Training must match the demands of the activity
Training should be varied to avoid boredom
questions.explain: Specificity means training should be relevant to the sport and the components of fitness it requires.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cool-down after exercise?
options: To gradually lower heart rate and remove waste products
questions.explain: A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and helps remove lactic acid, reducing stiffness.

questions.q: Fartlek training is best described as:
options: Training at a constant steady pace
Short maximal sprints with full rest
questions.explain: Fartlek, meaning 'speed play', varies intensity and terrain, developing both aerobic and anaerobic fitness.

questions.q: Which training method involves explosive bounding, hopping and jumping to develop power?
questions.explain: Plyometric training uses explosive movements to develop muscular power.

questions.q: The sit-and-reach test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: The multi-stage fitness test (bleep test) measures which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The bleep test estimates aerobic capacity, a measure of cardiovascular endurance.

questions.q: What do the letters FITT stand for?
questions.explain: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type - principles used to apply overload.

questions.q: Which method involves periods of work followed by periods of rest or recovery?
questions.explain: Interval training alternates bouts of work with rest periods.

questions.q: The principle that fitness gains are lost when training stops is known as:
questions.explain: Reversibility means fitness levels decline if training is stopped or reduced.

options: The range of movement at a joint
The maximum force a muscle can exert
The ability to keep going without tiring
questions.explain: Power combines strength and speed, e.g. an explosive jump or sprint start.

questions.q: Using the formula 220 - age, what is the maximum heart rate of a 16-year-old?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 16 = 204 bpm.
